slides.say: In the accompanying figure, four lines intersect at one point. Which expression equals x?

slides: What makes this question hard? Every angle is given with a letter, not a number. That's the main way exam geometry questions are made harder. [short pause] We'll solve it three ways, the math way, by plugging in numbers instead of the letters, and with an insight, for those who see it.

slides.say: [short pause] The math way first. We need x, and there are many letters, so we need an anchor, a known total. That's either a full turn, three hundred sixty degrees, or a straight angle, one hundred eighty.

Start with m. The angle right next to m fills the rest of a straight line together with m, so it's one hundred eighty minus m. In the same way, the angle next to n is one hundred eighty minus n, and the angle next to k is one hundred eighty minus k.
Now look at this slanted line. On one side of it there are exactly four angles, x and the three angles we just found. Together they make a straight angle, so they add up to one hundred eighty.
at: Now look at this slanted line
so they add up to one hundred eighty

slides.say: Here's our equation again. Careful with the brackets. There's a plus in front of each bracket, so we can just drop them.
at: so we can just drop them

slides.say: Now we need one tool from algebra. An equation is like a balance. If we do the same thing to both sides, it stays true. For example, five plus two equals seven. Subtract two from both sides, and we get five equals seven minus two. Still true, five is five. So a number that's added on one side can move to the other side as a minus.

Back to our equation. First, subtract one hundred eighty from both sides. On the right, one hundred eighty minus one hundred eighty is zero. On the left, we lose one of the three one hundred eighty terms.
at: On the left, we lose one

slides.say: Next, add m, n and k to both sides. On the left, minus m plus m is zero, and the same for n and k. So one hundred eighty plus one hundred eighty plus x equals m plus n plus k. That's three hundred sixty plus x.
at: That's three hundred sixty plus x

slides.say: Last, subtract three hundred sixty from both sides. So x equals m plus n plus k, minus three hundred sixty. Choice number four is our answer. Once you see the straight angle, the math is short. The hard part is seeing it on the last question of the section.
at: Choice number four is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now plugging in numbers. The question was made harder by putting letters instead of numbers, so we put numbers back. Why is that allowed? The right expression equals x for every possible m, n and k, so it also equals x for one example that we choose. We find x in our example, and then a choice that gives a different value is out.

Which numbers? Easy numbers that the figure allows. We choose m equals one hundred forty, and the same one hundred forty for n and k. Using the same number everywhere makes the choices much easier to check later.

With numbers the neighbors are easy. The angle next to each one hundred forty is forty. Forty plus forty plus forty is a hundred twenty. With x they make a straight angle, so x is a hundred eighty minus a hundred twenty, which is sixty degrees, in our example. Sixty is more than zero, so our numbers really fit a possible figure.

Now put one hundred forty into each choice and look for sixty. Choice number one says m plus n plus k, minus one hundred eighty. Three times one hundred forty is four hundred twenty, minus one hundred eighty. That's far more than sixty, so it's out. Choice number two says m minus n plus k. One hundred forty minus one hundred forty is zero, plus one hundred forty is one hundred forty. Out. Choice number three says m minus n minus k. Zero minus one hundred forty is negative. Out.

Choice number four says m plus n plus k, minus three hundred sixty. Four hundred twenty minus three hundred sixty is exactly sixty. Three choices are out, so choice number four is our answer. One more check: the four choices gave four different values, two hundred forty, one hundred forty, a negative and sixty. If two choices had given the same value, we'd plug in again with other numbers.
at: so choice number four is our answer

slides.say: [pause] And the insight. Look at the three angles m, n and k together. m and k go around most of the turn, and n covers the rest, so together they cover the whole full turn, three hundred sixty degrees. But they overlap. The part where m and n overlap is exactly x, so x is counted twice.

It's the overlap rule from the segments question again. The pieces together are the whole turn, plus the overlap once more. So m plus n plus k is three hundred sixty plus x. Move the three hundred sixty to the other side, and x equals m plus n plus k minus three hundred sixty. Choice number four. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: So m plus n plus k
minus three hundred sixty. Choice number four
